questions.question: At which domain separation support level are application properties domain-aware as needed?

explanation.correct: At the Standard support level, application properties are domain-aware as needed. This level includes all aspects of Basic level support plus the ability for service providers to create or modify processes per customer, with the instance owner configuring MVP business logic per tenant.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Basic level focuses on data going into proper domains, not property domain-awareness
Enhanced level builds on Standard; property domain-awareness starts at Standard
Properties can be domain-aware starting at the Standard support level

source.excerpt: Standard - Includes all aspects of Basic level support. Application properties are domain-aware as needed.

questions.question: Which features are available in the extended domain separation functionality for Performance Analytics with the Domain Separation Support plugin? (Choose three)

explanation.correct: The extended functionality available in the Performance Analytics — Domain Separation Support plugin includes: (1) Hierarchical multi-domain configurations to group domains and control score collection, (2) Collect aggregate scores by combining scores from multiple domains in a domain configuration, and (3) Dashboard filtering by domain to show scores by domain or domain aggregate.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Automatic data backup is not a PA domain separation feature
Cross-instance domain replication is not a feature of the PA Domain Separation Support plugin

source.excerpt: Hierarchical multi-domain configurations, Collect aggregate scores, Dashboard filtering by domain. The extended functionality is available in the Performance Analytics — Domain Separation Support plugin.

questions.question:
Evaluate the following statements about domain separation in Event Management:

Statement 1: Impact calculation in Event Management is supported with segregation based on how CIs are segregated.

Statement 2: The discovery process automatically segregates CIs by domain in Event Management.

Which statements are TRUE?

explanation.correct: Statement 1 is TRUE: Impact calculation is supported in Event Management domain separation, with segregation based on the manner in which CIs are segregated. Statement 2 is FALSE: The discovery process does NOT segregate CIs by domain - this is explicitly noted as a limitation in the documentation.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Statement 2 is false; discovery does NOT segregate CIs by domain. Statement 1 is true about impact calculation.
Statement 2 is false; the discovery process does not automatically segregate CIs by domain
Statement 1 is true; impact calculation IS supported with CI-based segregation

source.excerpt: Impact calculation - Supported. Segregation is based on the manner in which CIs are segregated. Dynamic CI groups - Partially supported. Note: The discovery process does not segregate CIs by domain.

questions.question: Which API enables copying Performance Analytics records between different domains on the same instance?

explanation.correct: The PADomainUtils API enables you to copy Performance Analytics records between different domains on the same instance. This is useful for propagating PA configurations across domains.

wrongAnswers.explanation: GlideDomain is not the specific API for copying PA records between domains
DomainCopy is not a standard ServiceNow API for this purpose
GlideRecord is a general data access API, not specifically designed for PA domain copying

source.excerpt: PADomainUtils - Global: The PADomainUtils API enables you to copy Performance Analytics records between different domains on the same instance.

questions.question: A sample use case for Enhanced domain separation support level states: 'Tenant-customers of a shared environment must be able to modify the impact, urgency, or priority matrix to set priority within their domain.' This demonstrates which capability?

options.text: Tenant self-service configuration of business logic

explanation.correct: This sample use case demonstrates the Enhanced support level capability where tenants of the instance can configure minimum viable product (MVP) business logic and data parameters for themselves. The ability to modify the priority matrix within their domain is tenant self-service configuration.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Basic data separation doesn't allow tenants to modify business logic like priority matrices
This is tenant self-configuration, not service provider creating processes for customers (which is Standard level)
This is not about delegating global admin functions, but about tenants configuring their own domain business logic

source.excerpt: Enhanced - Sample use case: Tenant-customers of a shared environment must be able to modify the impact, urgency, or priority matrix to set priority within their domain.

questions.question: What support level does CMDB have for domain separation?

explanation.correct: CMDB has Standard level domain separation support. This includes all aspects of Basic level support, plus domain-aware application properties and business logic that allows service providers to create or modify processes per customer tenant.

wrongAnswers.explanation: CMDB does support domain separation
CMDB has Standard, not Basic support
Enterprise is not a standard domain separation support level

source.excerpt: Support level: Standard. Includes all aspects of Basic level support. Application properties are domain-aware as needed. Business logic: The service provider (SP) creates or modifies processes per customer.

questions.question: Which CMDB features support domain separation? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: CMDB Health and CMDB Query Builder both support domain separation. This allows domain-specific health monitoring and querying of configuration items within appropriate domain boundaries.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Global platform settings are instance-wide, not domain-separated
Instance time zone is a global setting

source.excerpt: The following topics provide details about domain separation in Configuration Management (CMDB) modules: Domain separation in CMDB Health, Domain separation and CMDB Query Builder, Domain separation and CMDB Identification and Reconciliation.

questions.question: Which domain separation support level means an application stores data in the global domain and has no domain awareness?

explanation.correct: At the 'Not supported' level, the application has no domain awareness and stores all data in the global domain, making it unsuitable for multi-tenant environments.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Baseline provides basic domain separation with the sys_domain field on key tables
Standard provides domain-separated processes and configurations
Enhanced provides full domain-specific customization capabilities

questions.question: What does it mean when an application has 'Standard' domain separation support?

options.text: The application cannot be used with domain separation
The application supports domain-separated data and processes, with most features working in a multi-tenant environment
The application requires a separate instance per tenant
The application only works in the global domain

explanation.correct: Standard support means the application's data and processes are domain-separated, with most features functioning correctly in a multi-tenant environment, though some advanced customizations may be limited.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Standard means it IS supported, with domain-separated data and processes
Standard support works within a single domain-separated instance
Standard support enables domain-specific data, not just global

questions.question: A service provider wants to use Vulnerability Response in a domain-separated environment. What should they check first?

options.text: If the application has enough licenses
The domain separation compatibility matrix to verify the support level and any limitations

explanation.correct: Before deploying any application in a domain-separated environment, administrators should check the domain separation compatibility matrix to understand the support level and known limitations.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Licensing is important but doesn't determine domain separation compatibility
MID Server configuration is an operational step, not a compatibility check
User count doesn't affect domain separation compatibility

questions.question: Which ITSM application has Enhanced domain separation support? (Choose two)

explanation.correct: Incident Management and Problem Management have Enhanced domain separation support, allowing domain-specific process customization including priority matrices and assignment rules.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Change Management has Standard support, not Enhanced
Visual Task Boards have limited domain separation support

questions.question: How does Service Catalog handle domain separation?

options.text: Catalogs and catalog items cannot be domain-separated
Catalogs, categories, and catalog items can be assigned to specific domains, controlling visibility per tenant
Each tenant must have a completely separate Service Catalog instance
Service Catalog ignores domain separation entirely

explanation.correct: Service Catalog supports domain separation — catalogs, categories, and catalog items can be assigned to specific domains, controlling which tenants can see and request which items.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Service Catalog has domain separation support for items, categories, and catalogs
Domain separation eliminates the need for separate instances
Service Catalog is domain-aware and respects domain boundaries

questions.question: A service provider discovers that a specific ServiceNow application they need has only 'Baseline' domain separation support. What does this imply for their implementation?

options.text: They cannot use the application at all
The application has basic domain data separation but may lack domain-specific process customization for individual tenants
The application will work exactly like one with Enhanced support
They need to purchase additional plugins

explanation.correct: Baseline support means the sys_domain field exists on key tables for data separation, but the application may not support domain-specific process customization or configurations per tenant.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Baseline applications can still be used, just with limited domain-specific features
Baseline has fewer domain-specific features than Enhanced
Support level is inherent to the application, not a plugin purchase

questions.question: Which plugin extends domain separation support for Performance Analytics?

explanation.correct: The Domain Support for Performance Analytics plugin (com.snc.pa.domain) extends PA with domain-specific capabilities including domain-separated indicators, breakdowns, and dashboards.

wrongAnswers.explanation: This is the base MSP extensions plugin, not specific to Performance Analytics
PA Premium is a licensing tier, not a domain separation plugin
ITSM Domain Support is not the plugin name for PA domain separation

questions.question: What is the impact of using an application that does NOT support domain separation in a domain-separated instance?

options.text: Data from all tenants may be visible to all users of that application, creating potential data leakage
Only the admin user can access the application

explanation.correct: Applications without domain separation support store data in the global domain without domain boundaries, potentially exposing one tenant's data to users in other domains.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The instance continues to function; the issue is data visibility
Applications don't automatically gain domain awareness
Access isn't restricted to admin; it's that domain boundaries aren't enforced

questions.question: Which ServiceNow application has the HIGHEST level of domain separation support?

explanation.correct: Incident Management has full (Enhanced) domain separation support, including domain-separated workflows, SLAs, and assignment rules.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Knowledge Management has standard domain separation support but not the highest level
Performance Analytics has limited domain separation support
Project Portfolio Management has basic domain separation support

questions.question: What is a key consideration when implementing domain separation for the Service Catalog?

options.text: Catalog items cannot be shared across domains
Catalog items in the global domain are available to all child domains
Each domain must have completely separate catalog categories
Variable sets are not supported with domain separation

explanation.correct: Service Catalog items created in the global domain are visible across all child domains, while domain-specific items are only visible within their domain. This allows shared and tenant-specific catalog offerings.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Items CAN be shared by placing them in the global domain
Categories can be shared through the global domain; complete separation is not required
Variable sets do support domain separation
